What’s new in recent releases

v0.5.2

Transfers

  • A progress window for every copy. A transfer that runs longer than a second opens a floating window with From and To, progress, time left, Pause, Cancel and Hide, and asks its conflict questions there; while it prepares, it shows what it has found so far. General ▸ Transfers lets you choose this window, the Transfers list, or nothing.
  • Faster SFTP. Folders of small files download several times faster, large files and the viewer read faster over slow links, and servers whose only host key is RSA can now be reached.

Improvements

  • The Trash in the Left Side Bar. Favorites end with a Trash row; right-click it to Empty Trash, with progress and Cancel.
  • Double-clicking a file on a connection downloads it and opens it in its default app, as a local file does.
  • Network says when macOS has Local Network access turned off for MFCommander and offers Grant Access, instead of listing computers as "Not responding".
  • The Path Bar always shows the current folder in narrow Panels, and clicking a compact Path Bar opens the path field.

Bug Fixes

  • Pause and Cancel in the Transfers list respond while a copy is reporting progress.
  • An SMB address with a port, such as smb://host:1445/share, keeps its port.
  • The Left Side Bar keeps its scroll position and folded sections when it refreshes.
  • Selected file names, activity badges, the Filter placeholder and Disk Usage charts are easier to read in every theme.

v0.5.1

Improvements

  • Disk Usage keeps every scanned folder available to expand after a scan finishes or stops.
  • Blue Next items and Previous items links let you move forward and backward through large folders in Disk Usage.

Bug Fixes

  • Scanning a drive's root now includes the space used by folders that earlier summaries left out of the total.
  • A lone file in Disk Usage stays visible by name instead of appearing as "Other (1 file summarized)".

v0.5.0

Network

  • Browse your local network. A new Network section in the Left Side Bar lists the Macs, NAS drives and Windows PCs around you and opens any of them in a Panel. Browsing is free; opening a share needs Pro.
  • Everything a computer offers, in one list. Its SMB shares and NFS exports appear by name with a Kind column for each, and its SFTP and FTP servers open at their root.
  • Connect to Server opens a computer the network did not announce: type its address and pick the protocol.
  • Network asks for a password only when a share needs one, can remember it in your Keychain, and can save a share you browsed as a connection.

Improvements

  • Preview shows files on SMB shares: their details, the start of a text file, image and document previews, and video posters and audio details. Remote folders reach Get Info and Calculate too.
  • Deleting duplicates in Duplicate Files checks the files in the background, with progress and a Stop button.
  • Secondary text, chart lines and detail chips are easier to read in every theme.

Bug Fixes

  • The Modified column is wide enough for the full date and time again, and resizing it redraws every row.
  • Saving edited YAML in Kubernetes applies your edits with kubectl 1.33, instead of reporting success without changing anything.
  • On macOS 27, Settings ▸ Privacy reports Full Disk Access instead of "Could not check", and the Toolbar stays one color with the Right Side Bar open.
  • The path bar never widens the window, and drops whole folders from the middle instead of squeezing every name.
  • A tab whose folder has gone stays put and says so, and Reload brings the folder back once it returns.
  • Switch Focus moves the keyboard from the terminal back to the active Panel.
  • SFTP connections close once nothing is using them.

v0.4.3

Licensing

  • Activating while offline works at once and finishes the next time the Mac is online. A network or service problem never deactivates a Mac your license is active on.

Improvements

  • Back and Forward return to the Kubernetes cluster or Docker engine a location was shown on.
  • Files and folders that an SMB server exposes as links, as Windows does, now open and copy.
  • A Kubernetes port forward's connection count updates without redrawing the whole list.

Bug Fixes

  • Following the logs of a quiet pod or container stops when MFCommander quits.
  • Opening a cluster or engine while a folder was still loading no longer swaps the tab back to that folder.
  • A tab for a feature your license no longer includes is closed instead of left on screen.

v0.4.2

Bug Fixes

  • Fixed copying folders that contain links.
  • Fixed archives with symlinks that produced empty files.
  • Fixed scenarios where SFTP connections would fail. A refused key MFCommander remembered can now be cleared with Forget Host Key… from the Panel's banner or the connection editor.
  • Removing a Kubernetes cluster also removes any open tabs to that cluster.
  • Fixed SMB folder copies that failed when a file name included : or \.
  • Deleting a Dropbox connection now removes its grant from your Dropbox account.
  • Deleting a OneDrive connection now explains how to remove its grant from your Microsoft account.

v0.4.1

  • Choose the Terminal's font in Settings ▸ Terminal, including patched fonts such as Nerd Fonts, so shell prompt icons draw correctly.
  • Use Option as Meta now takes effect. It is off by default, so in the Terminal, Option types @, brackets, and the other characters your keyboard layout puts on Option.
  • The Bell setting is honored: Visual flashes the Terminal briefly, Sound plays the system beep, and Off stays silent.
  • The Move to Trash confirmation's button is blue from the start instead of red for a moment.
  • Escape cancels the Copy, Move, New Folder, Archive, and Move to Trash sheets, and the confirmations for Kubernetes detail actions, closing a busy Terminal, and quitting during a file operation.
  • The Console item in the window's Status Bar no longer cuts off its label.
  • When the window title is truncated, hovering over it shows the full location.
  • The Search pane's idle instruction wraps instead of clipping in a narrow pane.
  • Choosing a pod in the Kubernetes aggregated logs' source filter shows its logs instead of an empty viewer.

v0.4.0

  • A built-in Terminal. Open several terminal sessions at once along the bottom of the window, each running a shell on your Mac or inside a Kubernetes Pod or Docker container.
  • Forward Kubernetes ports. Port Forward… on a Pod, Service, Deployment, StatefulSet, DaemonSet, or ReplicaSet makes it reachable at a local address. When the Pods behind a forward are replaced, it reconnects on the same local port. The new Port Forwards tab lists every forward with Open, Copy, Stop, and Retry.
  • One Bottom Drawer for activity. Console, Transfers, Operation History, Port Forwards, and Terminal are now tabs in a drawer along the bottom of the window. View ▸ Show Bottom Drawer opens and closes it, and every tab except Terminal can still pop out to its own window.
  • Messages is now called Console. Click a message to see its full detail, with Copy and Show in Panel, and filter the list by level.
  • A Status Bar along the bottom of the window opens each Drawer tab and shows what needs attention: unread problems, unfinished transfers, and live port forwards. Right-click it to hide items, or turn it off in the View menu.
  • Each Panel has its own Path Bar and Status Bar. The Path Bar carries a Filter for the Panel's list, plus Favorite, Refresh, and View controls. The Status Bar shows the item count, the size of the selection, and free space.
  • A simpler toolbar: Left Side Bar, Connect, Search, Disk Usage, Duplicate Files, and Right Side Bar. Right-click the toolbar and choose Customize Toolbar… to add Back, Forward, Refresh, or Terminal.
  • A new Go menu with Enclosing Folder, Home, Go to Folder…, Connect…, and Recent Locations.
  • Add and edit connections without leaving the window. The + on a Left Side Bar section, New Connection… in the toolbar's Connect menu, and Edit Connection… on a connection's context menu open a sheet over the main window.
  • The Function Bar follows what the Panel shows. On Kubernetes, F4 edits a resource's YAML and F8 deletes it. On Docker, F8 removes the selected item.
  • Dates in listings fit their column instead of being cut off, with the full date in the tooltip. Turn off ISO dates in listings in Settings ▸ General to use your Mac's regional format.
  • Names sort in natural order, so file2 comes before file10.
  • With Calculate Directory Sizes on, sorting by Size orders folders by their calculated size.
  • Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ Row Style draws no borders, vertical lines, horizontal lines, or a full grid between rows.

v0.3.0

  • File operations run in the background. Copying, moving, deleting, and creating archives no longer lock the window. The new Transfers window shows each job's progress, speed, and time left, with Pause, Resume, and Cancel, and cancelling no longer leaves a partial file behind. Jobs on the same disk or connection take turns; others run side by side.
  • Undo file operations. Edit ▸ Undo (⌘Z) reverses your last copy, move, rename, or Move to Trash, and Window ▸ Operation History rolls back earlier ones, even days later. Every file is checked first, and anything that has changed since is skipped and explained. History stays on this Mac for 30 days unless you change or clear it in Settings ▸ General.
  • Answer file conflicts once. Choose Skip, Replace, Replace If Older, or Keep Both before a transfer starts, or answer in Transfers with Apply to all. A conflict no longer stops the whole app.
  • Merges folders that already exist at the destination. A bulk Replace now merges too, so it no longer discards files that only the destination had.
  • Browse an iPhone or iPad connected by USB, in every edition. It appears under Devices in the sidebar: copy photos and videos off it, copy files to and from apps that share documents, and rename, create folders, or delete where iOS allows.
  • Messages, Transfers, and Operation History now sit together in the toolbar. Messages and Transfers show a count, and Transfers flags a job waiting for your answer.
  • The status bar shows the free space on the listed disk, including SMB shares, and no longer reports a selected folder as "Zero KB".
  • Settings ▸ Privacy can ask macOS for Files & Folders and Local Network access, so MFCommander appears in those System Settings lists, and shows whether Full Disk Access is on.
  • Opens S3 folders holding more than 1,000 objects one page at a time, with First and Next. Sorting and filtering apply to the page shown.
  • Stays responsive with very large data: sorting huge folders, finding duplicates, scanning disks with millions of folders, and refreshing clusters with thousands of Pods.
  • Explains Kubernetes permission problems at once. View Logs and the Logs tab no longer open an empty viewer after a long wait, and a related resource you cannot read no longer takes you away from the one you were viewing.
  • Makes Kubernetes more dependable on busy clusters. Events and other slow lists now finish loading instead of being restarted by automatic refresh, and a failed log stream is reported in the viewer and in Messages rather than ending as though the Pod had stopped logging.

v0.2.13

  • Ejects removable drives directly from the sidebar.
  • Shows which iCloud files are stored only in the cloud, and downloads one when you click its cloud icon. The icon disappears once the file is on your Mac.
  • Filters Kubernetes resources by status, using the choices present in the loaded list. Status and namespace filters now sit together above column headers that match the file listings.
  • Keeps your selected detail tab when a Kubernetes resource refreshes, and holds your position when its contents have not changed.
  • Copies selected Message Log rows with right-click Copy or ⌘C.
  • Asks for confirmation before Move to Trash from a file's context menu.
  • Fixes a failed remote connection check letting a transfer start anyway, which skipped the overwrite prompt that protects files at the destination.
  • Blocks pending Kubernetes changes when read-only mode is turned on while an action is already running.
  • Fixes cloud connections failing when several operations needed to renew a sign-in at the same time.
  • Uses less memory during Kubernetes monitoring and after a remote media viewer closes.
  • Keeps recent history when following a remote log for a long time, within a fixed disk limit.
  • Shows the first 20,000 results of a large file search while continuing to count every match.
  • Removes the CPU and memory debugging display from the toolbar.

v0.2.12

  • Browses Kubernetes custom resources directly from the sidebar, grouped by API, with the columns your cluster defines.
  • Follows more connections between workloads, networking, storage, permissions, and configuration, including Argo CD and Flux managers.
  • Reads container health more easily, with clearer summaries, condition timelines, and events.
  • Shows current, average, and peak readings on the usage charts.
  • Keeps large-cluster overviews and resource counts working, and uses less memory while refreshing them.
  • Lists active ReplicaSets by default, with an option to show inactive ones and sidebar counts that match the choice.
  • Follows live logs more reliably.
  • Reads multiline fields in compact view.
  • Shows the log controls clearly in every theme.
  • Revisits application messages in the new Message Log, with links back to where each came from.

v0.3.0

  • File operations run in the background. Copying, moving, deleting, and creating archives no longer lock the window.
